clue.text: Being displayed at less than one exhibition

indicators.note: less than the whole word one means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an exhibition is a show

explanation.surface: Something is on view at fewer than a single exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' trims the last letter from ONE, leaving ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Items being displayed in a gallery are said to be on view in a show, the idiom for exhibited.

clue.text: Undoubtedly without demand for an answer

explanation.surface: Certainly, and nobody is asking for a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means certainly as an idiom, and literally describes a situation with nothing asked of anyone.

clue.text: Way to apply a suspended sentence

definitions.text: Way to apply a suspended sentence

parts.words: Way to apply a suspended sentence
parts.note: a suspended sentence sounds like a lenient court ruling, but here it is a death sentence carried out by suspending the convict from a rope

explanation.surface: A legal question about how a suspended sentence is put into effect.
explanation.walkthrough: A suspended sentence in law is one not served; the clue reads it as a sentence of execution by rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital punishment by rope is the literal way to leave a condemned person suspended.

clue.text: Waterproof vessel

explanation.surface: A boat that keeps water out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a weatherproof outdoor jacket and a large square-rigged sailing ship of the merchant era.

clue.text: Mark the starting-point

explanation.surface: An instruction to note where a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A light score on a surface is one sense; the other is the line from which runners begin, as in starting from nothing.

clue.text: Cleric be supporting Jack

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits below, so it comes after the sailor

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the crossword abbreviation for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman is told to back up a sailor called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts BE below AB in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A French priest or monk is addressed by this title, so it names a churchman.

clue.text: Daisy perhaps needs taming in the field?

definitions.text: Daisy perhaps needs taming in the field?

parts.words: Daisy perhaps needs taming in the field?
parts.note: a daisy growing untended in a meadow is an uncultivated bloom, and the joke reads that as an unruly creature that must be tamed

explanation.surface: Someone called Daisy is unruly out in the countryside and needs settling.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, growing uncultivated.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy found in a field is an uncultivated plant blooming naturally rather than in a garden.

clue.text: Short time Seth might have included to process corn

indicators.note: have included means the anagrammed letters take the hour abbreviation inside them
might signals that the letters of Seth could be rearranged into another order

parts.note: HR is the short form of hour, a time

explanation.surface: Seth briefly includes something in order to deal with the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' rearranges the name into TESH, and 'have included' takes the hour abbreviation inside, straight after the T; Seth looks like the person doing the threshing.
explanation.definitionFit: Separating grain from husks by beating is the farm task of processing a cereal crop.

clue.text: Very gradually putting one part of foot alongside another

parts.note: a foot contains twelve inches, so an inch is one part of it
by means beside or alongside
another part of the foot, a second inch

explanation.surface: Advice to walk slowly, setting one bit of the foot next to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' suggests the body part; it is the twelve-inch length.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancing a tiny unit at a time is the idiom for slow, step-by-step progress.

clue.text: Imprisoned beast getting in a stew

parts.note: jugged is slang for jailed, jug being prison
a hare is a wild animal

explanation.surface: A caged animal gets itself into a fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' reads as flustered; the dish is a traditional British casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic British dish of game slowly cooked in a pot or jug is a kind of stew.

clue.text: Drop off nearly twelve

indicators.note: nearly means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: a dozen is twelve

explanation.surface: Someone nods off at almost midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' removes the N from DOZEN; 'twelve' suggests a clock time.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off is to fall into a light sleep, the sense of dropping off.

clue.text: Disheartened doorkeeper's employer

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word goes

parts.note: an usher keeps a door at a court or theatre

explanation.surface: A dejected porter's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes H, the middle letter of USHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who employs a tool or service makes use of it, so an employer here is one who utilises.

clue.text: One of the family included a kiss, as a result there is less tension

indicators.note: included means the family member takes the next pieces inside

parts.note: a relation is a family member
X is the conventional symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: A relative gets a kiss, and things become calmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts A and X inside RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosening up means easing of strain, a state with reduced tautness.

clue.text: Finish off associate in crime soundly

indicators.note: soundly means the partner's title is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: an accomplice is a partner in crime

explanation.surface: A criminal kills off a partner thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly'; it signals a near sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To complete a task is to bring it to an end successfully.

clue.text: Young lady taken on for cricket term

parts.note: a maiden is a young unmarried woman
over means on top of, as on does

explanation.surface: A girl is hired to explain a cricket word.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; a maiden is one with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a set of six deliveries with no runs conceded has this name.

clue.text: Chaplain?

parts.note: a chaplain conducts church services and may also serve with the armed forces, so either sense of service fits

explanation.surface: A one-word query about a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A military chaplain is a member of the forces, and also a man who leads worship.

clue.text: Ambassador almost gets degree

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: an ambassador is a diplomat

explanation.surface: An envoy nearly earns a university qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate awarded on completing a course of study is a qualification like a degree.

clue.text: Time in town in Hertfordshire making metal containers

parts.note: taken as written
Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London

explanation.surface: Someone spends time in a Hertfordshire town producing tin cans.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods such as pots and cans made of thin plated iron form this category of kitchen ware.

clue.text: Vote not to

parts.note: read as an instruction, it means choose not to cast any ballot at all

explanation.surface: A motion to reject something in a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as voting against; it means declining to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Formally declining to cast a ballot is refraining from voting.

clue.text: In old gold can be unyielding

parts.note: taken as written
ex means former
or is the heraldic word for gold
able to be is the sense of can be

explanation.surface: Gold of an earlier era can be firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Relentless and impossible to persuade or stop is the sense of not giving way.

clue.text: Period spent batting was early enough

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
a period is a time

explanation.surface: A batter's time at the crease was punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving before a deadline is being punctual, not late.

clue.text: Regretting stopping short — bankruptcy

indicators.note: stopping short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ruing means regretting

explanation.surface: Someone regrets halting early before going bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial collapse leaves a person destitute, the state of being ruined.

clue.text: Sharp-tasting pie that does not have a crust on top

definitions.text: pie that does not have a crust on top

explanation.surface: A sour pie with no lid of pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic in flavour is one sense; an open pastry case with filling and no lid is the other.

clue.text: Not bothered about double turn

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the next two words are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone unfazed by a double twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Being calm and unworried means having no cares disturbing one.

clue.text: Some awful name given to skeletal part

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dreadful name has been given to a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'given to skeletal part' as the definition; 'given to' is a link and only 'skeletal part' can replace a bone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two forearm bones is part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Summon but not on stream

indicators.note: but not means the following word is removed from the summoning word

parts.note: to beckon is to summon with a gesture
taken as written

explanation.surface: Call for someone, though not while on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: BECK is a northern English word for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brook in northern England is a kind of stream.

clue.text: Name a noisy sort dressing

indicators.note: sort means arrange, so the letters before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Identify a loud kind of salad topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun after 'noisy'; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-and-oil sauce is used as a salad topping.

clue.text: Stopping without starting and doing some gardening

indicators.note: without starting means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: braking is stopping a vehicle

explanation.surface: Halting without setting off, and working in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a toothed tool over lawn or soil is a gardening task.
